A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research objectives, experiments, and appendices A–B. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original symmetry-detection results, component ablations, and rotation-robustness analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative comparisons, and rotation-robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.3, Equation 21 replaces the original feature terms with r_Q^n(F), explicitly applying whole-neighborhood rotation in spatial reflectional matching. This locally revises the specified computation; the architecture, losses, orientational anchors, and rotational matching remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on DENDI for reflection and rotation symmetry, and evaluate reflection symmetry on SDRW and LDRS. The rotated-input test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain PMCNet and EquiSym for reflection detection and EquiSym for rotation detection. The component-ablation and non-equivariant comparison variants are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the augmentation to 30k training images, D8-equivariant ResNet-34, 100 epochs, batch size 32, and optimizer schedule. The sAP thresholds, dilated-axis F1 evaluation, and rotation-RMSE procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same orientational-anchor and matching-kernel ablations, padding-sensitivity analysis, rotation-equivariance tests, qualitative examples, and observation about confusion between two-fold and four-fold symmetry.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The results retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the empirical figures retain their values and findings. For example, Table 3 reports the same reflection F1 scores of 68.3, 43.4, and 37.2 on SDRW, LDRS, and DENDI, and rotation F1 of 26.8 on DENDI.

T1.justification: Equation 21 revises the mathematical definition of spatial reflectional similarity, and the accompanying sentence defines r_Q^n as rotating the entire neighborhood about its center. Appendices A–B remain unchanged, including the spatial-equivariance derivation, which does not incorporate this added operator explicitly.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about axis-level detection, dihedral-equivariant representations, orientational anchors, specialized matching, and superior benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of ablation gains, rotation robustness, the SDRW comparison, and precision–recall behavior are unchanged. The proposed extensions to continuous groups, 3D spaces, and varying viewpoints are also retained without new applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The implementation section retains the same augmentation recipe, group-convolution description, model, hyperparameters, and training schedule. The project link is unchanged, and no hardware, runtime, or additional code/data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The same 63 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against heatmap-based methods and earlier equivariant approaches does not change.

P1.justification: A short explanatory clause defining neighborhood rotation is added after Equation 21, and the arXiv version/date header changes. The remaining prose, section order, and narrative structure are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 receive localized label and grouping edits, including revised channel-pair highlighting in Figure 3 and neighborhood-rotation notation in Figure 4. Table 3 moves between columns, and later text and references reflow. No empirical figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The explicit neighborhood-rotation definition and diagram refinements improve clarity locally. However, Equation 21 adds an operation while Appendix B.2 retains the earlier derivation without explaining how it applies to the revised expression. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects an omitted description or changes the evaluated computation, leaving the net effect on technical quality uncertain.
